candidate.hypothesis: When an input changes, we must include the changed input and all downstream nodes reachable via edges, following the dependency chain without revisiting or traversing unknown items.
candidate.sql: SELECT DISTINCT e.downstream FROM edge e JOIN changed c ON e.input = c.name WHERE e.downstream IN (SELECT name FROM node WHERE name IN (SELECT input FROM edge WHERE input IN (SELECT name FROM changed))) UNION SELECT name FROM changed

method.hypothesis: Cases with known mismatches (failed=1) in small input sizes (size ≤ 10) and distinct families are most informative; prioritize cases where output size differs significantly from input size, indicating strong dependency or transformation behavior.
method.sql: SELECT DISTINCT id FROM feedback WHERE failed = 1 AND size <= 10 AND outputs > 0 ORDER BY ABS(outputs - size) DESC, family DESC

selection.hypothesis: The 'impact' problem addresses a critical bottleneck in maintaining accurate and up-to-date product evidence, which is essential for reliable decision-making.
